I had a call center position at my last job. I had done extremely well and began handling other responsibilities. I had the recommendation of my department's director and a letter of commendation from the CEO for having handled a difficult and important situation.

I applied for some internal positions. The first position I applied for was directly related to my call center position, it was considered entry level and it was office work filing papers and such. I got pretty far in the process, but the job was ultimately given to a 21 year old with only 2 months experience as an intern. I had been working in a related position for 4 years.

The second position was in a different part of the company, but it was in something that I had a lot of experience with before I had begun working there. The person who interviewed me told me when we started that he had not read my resume and that he did not think I was what he was looking for. When I mentioned my professional and relevant experience, he brought up some other "requirements" that he thought I probably lacked, but I had those too. After that he asked "is there anything else you'd like to talk about" whenever he finished a sentence, so I took the hint and left.

Anything that happens two times is the beginning of a pattern and I wasnt stupid enough to wait for the third time. I applied at other places in the business and wound up with a 20% raise and way more opportunities within a few weeks. At the exit interview I told them that I was hoping that there would be more opportunity to move up, especially given my qualifications and the HR Manager replied "well, you did move up from part time to full time the first year you were here."

I used to have job loyalty. Now the only way I would work at the old company would be as a mercenary. I would take the highest possible salary from them while continuing to look for other jobs elsewhere.

C'est la vie. Shit happens.
